transcript.said:
Chen & Associates CPA, a four-person accounting firm in Richmond BC. Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00,
plus Saturdays 10:00-14:00 from Feb 1 to Apr 30 only. English and Mandarin.

Clients come to us or meet on video — nobody goes out. Three CPAs and one bookkeeper.

Money. A personal tax return is CAD 120 for a simple one, CAD 250 with rental or
self-employment income. A corporate year-end starts at CAD 1,800 and is always quoted by a
CPA after seeing the books, never over chat. A first consultation is 30 minutes free.
Bookkeeping is CAD 90/hour. Late-filing situations carry no surcharge from us.

What we will not take on: US tax filings (we refer to a cross-border firm), anything
involving a CRA audit already in progress (that needs a tax lawyer, we say so), and
crypto trading gains — we do not have the expertise and say so plainly.

Decisions a person must always make: whether a situation is complex enough to need a CPA
rather than the bookkeeper. Any question that amounts to tax advice — never answered by
the agent, always booked into the free consultation instead.

Who work goes to: Michelle, the office manager, on Telegram.

Deadlines matter more than in most businesses. Personal returns are due April 30; a client
messaging on April 25 about a return not started is a different conversation from one
messaging in July, and the agent should say so and get them booked sooner.

After: 24 hours after an appointment, check with Michelle that it happened and what the
client is waiting on from us.


That is everything I have. Ask only what you genuinely cannot infer and what a customer
would actually hear — do not ask me to read the brief back. If something is missing that
you can flag as an assumption instead, flag it and carry on.
transcript.replied:
Read the tool kit. Two things I can't infer, both about the ordinary case:

**1. The routine personal return — what actually happens?** Someone messages in March: "I need my 2025 taxes done, nothing complicated." Does that end in an appointment (in-person or video) at a time the agent picks, or does it end in "send us your slips" — a portal, an email, a drop-off — with no meeting at all? I'd like the ordinary path walked through, because that's the one most of the traffic takes and it decides whether the flow ends in a diary entry or a handover to Michelle.

**2. Who holds the diary?** Three CPAs and a bookkeeper — is there one shared calendar the agent can book into directly, or does Michelle place everything herself and the agent's job is to hand her a request? And when it *is* a booking: does the client pick their CPA, or do they get whoever's free?

transcript.said: Assume anything still open and mark it in the plan's open questions. Write PLAN.md.
transcript.replied:
`PLAN.md` is written. Nothing else — no flow.yaml, no rules, no tools.

The shape of it:

**Eighteen nodes, seven endings.** Greeting → identify → (new / existing / no number) → what they need → route → either one of three declines, or the personal-return path, or the consultation path — both of which converge on the same diary tail.

**The one design decision worth arguing about.** The firm's two "a person must decide this" rules — *is it complex enough for a CPA*, and *what's the answer to this tax question* — did not become handover nodes. Both resolve to the same move: book the free half hour with a CPA. And "never assign the bookkeeper" is enforced by `diary.find_slots` only ever searching CPA diaries, so there is no argument on the tool that could name them. A rule the code can refuse, the code refuses.

**`deadline_check` is its own node**, not a sentence inside the booking step, because 25 April and July being different conversations is the thing this business named explicitly — and folded into the diary lookup it is exactly the sentence that gets dropped.

**Seven kit tools unchanged, nine written.** The kit is shaped around somebody driving to an address; here nobody goes out, so the calendar, the create-customer and the notify tools all need replacing. `rules.deadline_pressure` does the date arithmetic so the model never does.

**Thirteen open questions**, and three of them block scenarios: the cross-border firm's number (read out to a customer, so I did not invent one), the Mandarin wording of the refusals, and whether there is a documents-only path for a plain T4 return with no meeting. That last one is the assumption I'd least like to be wrong — if a meeting isn't how a simple return starts, that's a branch, not a tweak.
